title: Four Australian universities are rolling out ChatGPT Edu
friendlyTitle: Four Australian universities are giving students ChatGPT Edu
summary: OpenAI says UNSW, the University of Sydney, La Trobe, and Adelaide University are giving students and staff ChatGPT Edu, on staggered timelines. A survey OpenAI commissioned of 1,018 Australian students, taken 3–7 August, found 81% already use AI several times a week, and 28% say they have built an agent. UNSW is extending access toward more than 80,000 people.
friendlySummary: UNSW, the University of Sydney, La Trobe, and Adelaide University are rolling out ChatGPT Edu to students and staff, on different schedules. In a survey OpenAI paid for, 81% of students said they already use AI several times a week.
whyItMatters: For a student, the practical change is institutional access plus a rule for when AI is allowed. UNSW's Can, Can't, Must labels are the part that changes daily work: a task can permit AI, ban it, or require it. The usage figures are from a company-commissioned survey, not an independent census.
friendlyWhyItMatters: The useful change is not just access. UNSW can mark a task as one where AI is allowed, banned, or required. The survey numbers come from OpenAI, so treat them as the company's own research.
